subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice,**

The manager told the employees that their hard work had been noticed and that they would be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which would be an acknowledgement of their dedication.

options.text: "Your hard work has been noticed and you will be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which will be an acknowledgement of your dedication," the manager said to the employees.
"Your hard work was noticed and you will be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which is an acknowledgement of your dedication," the manager said to the employees.
"Your hard work had been noticed and you would be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which would be an acknowledgement of your dedication," the manager said to the employees.
"Their hard work had been noticed and they would be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which was an acknowledgement of their dedication," the manager said to the employees.

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. "Your hard work has been noticed and you will be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which will be an acknowledgement of your dedication," the manager said to the employees. .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence requires conversion from indirect speech to direct speech while maintaining the correct tense and structure.
 
• In indirect speech, the sentence states that the manager told the employees about their hard work being noticed and a bonus being awarded as an acknowledgment.
 
• When converting to direct speech, the pronouns and tenses must align with the context and time frame of the original message.
 
• The correct option (1) uses the present perfect tense **"has been noticed"**, which matches the sense of the original indirect statement.
 
• It also uses the future tense **"will be given"** and **"will be an acknowledgment"** to indicate actions that are yet to happen, as expressed in the original sentence.

Correct sentence: *"Your hard work has been noticed and you will be given a bonus at the end of the quarter, which will be an acknowledgement of your dedication," the manager said to the employees.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Direct and Indirect Speech:**

 
 
• When converting from indirect to direct speech, ensure the pronouns, tenses, and time expressions are adjusted to match the context.
 
• For example, "their" becomes "your" and "they" becomes "you" in direct speech when the speaker is addressing the employees directly.
 
 
 
• **Why other options are incorrect:**
 
 
• Option 2: Uses "was noticed", which incorrectly changes the tense from present perfect to past simple.
 
• Option 3: Uses "had been noticed" and "would be given", which alters the original meaning and implies a hypothetical or past scenario rather than a future event.
 
• Option 4: Uses "their" and "they", which fails to align with the direct speech perspective where the manager is addressing the employees directly.
